head_commit.message:
Support inline model, reasoning, and speed selection in `/model` (#54378)

## What changed

Allow `/model [model] --reasoning <level> --speed <tier>` to update the current session without changing saved defaults. Both space-separated and `=` flag values are supported; omitting the model applies settings to the current model. Bare `/model` still opens the picker.

Validate model availability, supported reasoning levels, and speed tiers before applying changes. Reject unknown flags, duplicate settings, and missing values. Apply model, reasoning, and speed together after server acceptance.

Restore each thread's speed when switching threads, and use destination configuration defaults for new sessions instead of carrying over the active session's speed.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage for inline commands, invalid arguments, unchanged saved defaults, settings-only updates to hidden current models, destination speed defaults, and speed restoration on the next turn after switching threads.

head_commit.message:
Retry SQLite operations on transient writer contention (#54369)

## Why

Competing SQLite writers can cause database opening and writes to fail with `SQLITE_BUSY`. Deferred write transactions can also encounter contention after taking a read snapshot.

## What changed

- Add up to two retries with 100 ms and 200 ms delays for SQLite busy errors during pool opening, writer admission, and standalone writes.
- Use a shared `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` helper across state, thread history, and agent message board writes to acquire the writer slot before reading.
- Preserve bound arguments when retrying standalone writes, and commit writes using `RETURNING` before exposing their results. Retry transaction admission without replaying an already-started transaction.

## Testing

Add tests using real SQLite writer contention to verify recovery after a competing writer releases its lock. Queue tests cover enqueue, update, and delete, checking preserved payloads, single revision increments, and no duplicate messages or unintended deletions.

head_commit.message:
## New Features

- Open `/config` to search preferences across categories, change supported settings immediately, and see which changes require a restart. (#52990, #53429)
- Send a follow-up while Codex is responding to steer it immediately. Interrupting a turn also stops active Code Mode cells and their nested tool calls. (#51812, #51835)
- Configure a leader key in `/keymap`. The default is `Ctrl+X`, shortcut hints stay open until you choose or cancel, and voice mute moves to `F9`. (#52273)
- Restart a managed background server from `/daemon`. Codex warns about work the restart could interrupt, then reconnects automatically. (#53173)
- Codex can run independent read-only tools in parallel, including skill, memory, and conversation-history lookups. (#52245)
- Daybreak is enabled by default for eligible accounts. `codex exec` can also select it with an OpenAI API key when the server offers access. (#53701, #53717)

## Bug Fixes

- Resuming a saved thread restores its permissions and network approvals, while respecting explicit overrides and current managed policy. (#53150, #53419, #53424)
- The network proxy now checks permission before a DNS lookup, rejects duplicate `Host` headers, and prevents credential aliases from bypassing inspection hooks. (#51650, #52661, #53506)
- Return to an existing side conversation with `/side` after switching threads. Answers to pending prompts also go back to the thread that asked. (#52184, #53436)
- On Windows, `Ctrl+V` and `Shift+Insert` paste text as well as images. On WSL, repeated pastes reuse the clipboard reader, and copy attempts time out instead of hanging. (#53224, #52967, #53453)
- Local commands finish promptly when a child keeps an output pipe open. Remote commands preserve late-arriving output so the final poll can still collect it. (#52652, #53331, #53622)
- `codex exec` no longer prints the same file diff again after an unrelated command. (#53444)

## Documentation

- Updated the bundled OpenAI Docs guidance for migrations to the GPT-6 family, including model-specific reasoning, tool use, and data residency considerations. (#51768)
- Clarified how the Linux sandbox uses bubblewrap for filesystem isolation and seccomp for syscall filtering. (#52610)

## Chores

- Codex now uses its standard shell executor and no longer bundles a patched `zsh`. Configurations using the retired shell flags receive a migration notice. (#52160, #52213)
- Reduced Linux and macOS release package size by stripping symbols from packaged binaries while preserving them in the original build outputs. (#52178)

head_commit.message:
Retry SQLite operations on transient writer contention (#54369)

## Why

Competing SQLite writers can cause database opening and writes to fail with `SQLITE_BUSY`. Deferred write transactions can also encounter contention after taking a read snapshot.

## What changed

- Add up to two retries with 100 ms and 200 ms delays for SQLite busy errors during pool opening, writer admission, and standalone writes.
- Use a shared `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` helper across state, thread history, and agent message board writes to acquire the writer slot before reading.
- Preserve bound arguments when retrying standalone writes, and commit writes using `RETURNING` before exposing their results. Retry transaction admission without replaying an already-started transaction.

## Testing

Add tests using real SQLite writer contention to verify recovery after a competing writer releases its lock. Queue tests cover enqueue, update, and delete, checking preserved payloads, single revision increments, and no duplicate messages or unintended deletions.

head_commit.message:
Retry SQLite operations on transient writer contention (#54369)

## Why

Competing SQLite writers can cause database opening and writes to fail with `SQLITE_BUSY`. Deferred write transactions can also encounter contention after taking a read snapshot.

## What changed

- Add up to two retries with 100 ms and 200 ms delays for SQLite busy errors during pool opening, writer admission, and standalone writes.
- Use a shared `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` helper across state, thread history, and agent message board writes to acquire the writer slot before reading.
- Preserve bound arguments when retrying standalone writes, and commit writes using `RETURNING` before exposing their results. Retry transaction admission without replaying an already-started transaction.

## Testing

Add tests using real SQLite writer contention to verify recovery after a competing writer releases its lock. Queue tests cover enqueue, update, and delete, checking preserved payloads, single revision increments, and no duplicate messages or unintended deletions.

Add tests using real SQLite writer contention to verify recovery after a competing writer releases its lock. Queue tests cover enqueue, update, and delete, checking preserved payloads, single revision increments, and no duplicate messages or unintended deletions.

Prevent duplicate assistant messages around interleaved commands (#54365)

## Why

When a command starts before an assistant message completes, the TUI can flush the streamed text and then render it again when the completion arrives. This duplicates the preamble in both live output and replay.
